result.title: Look Ahead: Search-Driven Reasoning in Embodied AI
result.summary: Search allows a robotic policy to evaluate candidate futures before committing to an action. Motivated by test-time planning for vision-language action (VLA) models, we study selective search over action chunks in PushT using a frozen Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy. Beam search generates perturbed alternatives around the policy prediction and scores them through rollouts from cloned simulator states. Across 50 evaluation episodes, beam search raises task success from 0% to 18% and increases average cumulative reward from 39.44 to 103.2. We introduce One Step Ahead (OSA), a gate that simulates the nominal policy chunk and invokes full search only when its predicted coverage drop exceeds a threshold. In the reported ablations, OSA preserves or improves success while reducing runtime by approximately 3x relative to full beam search. Ablations over tree depth, branching factor, beam width, and replanning frequency show that larger search budgets do not consistently improve performance. The results support selective test-time search for action-chunking policies; evaluation on language-conditioned VLAs and physical robots remains future work.

AI.brief_summary: 在冻结的 ACT 动作分块策略上研究 PushT 任务的选择性测试时搜索：用 beam search 生成并模拟候选动作块，并引入 OSA 门控，仅在预测覆盖下降超阈值时才启动完整搜索。
AI.relevance_reason: 「何时额外搜索、何时停止」与增大搜索预算未必更好的结论，可供核查 LVR 中动态计算分配与停止决策的门控设计，但该文针对机器人动作搜索而非 VLM 内部 latent，迁移性需判断。
